answers.M8-S1: Mason bees can fly home really fast, even from two and a half miles away, and they still stop to collect pollen on the way.
answers.M8-S2: To show the bees had a hard trip because they had to fly low and couldn't see where they were going.
answers.M8-S3: The trip was easy for them, since they had time to stop and gather pollen and still got home quickly.
answers.M8-S4: So he could tell which bees were his when they came back to the nest.
answers.M8-S5: He thinks the bees won't make it home, but then he is excited and surprised when Aglaé says two came back fast.
answers.M8-S6: It tells how the bees got home quickly, starting with the author wanting to know about them and ending with the bees arriving with pollen.
answers.M8-S7: To show how fast the bees flew home, less than three quarters of an hour for two and a half miles.
answers.M8-S8: To show that marking the bees was hard and he got stung, so some bees got hurt.
answers.M8-S9: That they found their way home without seeing landmarks, so they must know the way some other way.
